note: The 2004 edition reduces the eulogy to the sole Theogenes
The 2004 edition joins the monks of Sinai (38) and of Raithu (43) in one eulogy (mr:0114-monachi-raithi); the historical editions print them as two eulogies.
The historical editions commemorate a bishop Euphrasius in Africa on this day; in the same eulogy the 2004 edition commemorates Euphrasius, bishop of Clermont (mr:0114-euphrasius).

edition_notes.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: "Whose birthday is the 7th of this month" seems to be an error, as this would point to Canute Lavard (mr:0107-canutus-lavard), who was not a king.

note: The 2004 eulogy mr:0123-clemens-et-agathangelus joins Clement and Agathangelus; the historical editions give Agathangelus a eulogy of his own.
The 1914 English fuses the eulogies of Ingenuinus and Albuinus of Brixen, which the 1749 edition and the 2004 edition print separately (mr:0205-ingenuinus, mr:0205-albuinus).
The 2004 edition has a single Valentine (on the via Flaminia), generally identified with the bishop of Terni; the 1749 and 1914 editions print both eulogies on this day.

The 1749 edition names Eleutherius, bishop, and 128 others in Persia on February 20; probably the eulogy of Sadoth, bishop, and 128 companions (mr:0218-sadoth-et-socii): same place, king (Sapor), number and refusal to adore the sun.

The 1749 and 1914 editions print the thirty-nine martyrs of the mines of Phaeno as a eulogy of their own, after that of Silvanus of Gaza; the 2004 edition commemorates them together with him in mr:0504-silvanus-et-socii.

edition_notes.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: 'Lucius' where the Latin has 'Mucii'.

note: The Hippolytus buried in the Ager Veranus is traditionally the Hippolytus of the 2004 eulogy mr:0813-pontianus-et-hippolytus, which leads with Pontian and tells a rewritten narrative.

edition_notes.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: This text is the rewritten eulogy of the Twelve Brothers of Benevento and does not name Donatus or Felix; it succeeds the 1749 eulogy, which mentions the twelve brothers' feast and Benevento, but its subject differs.

note: The 2004 edition reduces the eulogy to Quintus alone (mr:0905-quintus).

edition_notes.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: This text joins the Octave and the Seven Sorrows in one sentence, with no clean point to split it; the Seven Sorrows half corresponds to mr:0915-maria-perdolens.
Translation error: the 1749 Latin calls him 'Episcopi Abrincensis et Confessoris', not a martyr.

note: The 2004 edition drops Mark and leads with the three brothers.

edition_notes.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin is a translation of relics (Translatio), not a birthday.

note: The historical editions place Maximus at Apamea; the 2004 edition places him at Cumae (mr:1030-maximus).
